item.title: Compose
item.description:
wctr compose runs a multi-container application described by the Compose Specification, through the engine’s API. It is the separate module go-wasmcontainers/compose (v0.3.1, status M1), and it is built into wctr since cmd/wctr v0.1.0 (see Getting started); the standalone wctr-compose still exists. Compose files are accepted in three formats, YAML, JSON and HCL2, which load to the same model; files of different formats merge (-f compose.yaml -f override.hcl). The HCL2 mapping is specified in docs/HCL.md.

Commands

wctr compose [-f FILE]... [-p NAME] [--profile P]... COMMAND

Command Flags
up [SERVICE...] -d, --force-recreate, --build, --remove-orphans
down -v
ps [SERVICE...] -a, -q
logs [SERVICE...] -f
start, stop, restart dependencies first
rm [SERVICE...] -s
pull, images
build builds the services’ images with wctr build
config --format yaml|json|hcl, -q, --services

Loading is complete: discovery, interpolation, .env, merging, extends, include, profiles, and validation against the specification’s schema, with every error carrying file:line:column. The Compose files are untrusted input and every reader is bounded and fuzzed.

Networking (v0.3.0)

Services reach each other by service name and aliases, on as many networks as they declare. This needs engine v0.14.0 or later (it is built against v0.18.0). Builds (up --build, build) use wctr build (compose v0.2.0).

Limits

What the engine cannot do yet, and compose therefore does not:

  • ports and restart are accepted with a warning, not applied (no published ports, no restart policies).
  • service_healthy fails clearly: compose does not run health checks.
  • Build attributes such as remote contexts, cache_from and secrets are accepted with a warning and not applied; what the builder itself does not do is on the Build page.
  • No host bind mounts, and no file outside the project directory.
